name: NA-Semax Amidate

b.x: NA-Semax Amidate (N-Acetyl Semax Amidate, CAS pending) is a stabilized derivative of Semax with an estimated 3 to 5 times greater potency per microgram. Dolotov and colleagues showed the parent compound Semax produced a three-fold BDNF mRNA increase from a single dose in rat hippocampus [1], and NA-Semax Amidate pushes the pharmacokinetics further. The modification is straightforward. An N-terminal acetyl group blocks aminopeptidase degradation. A C-terminal amide cap blocks carboxypeptidase attack. The core sequence, ACTH(4-10) extended with Pro-Gly-Pro, stays identical to the parent compound approved in Russia for cognitive and neuroprotective indications. The result is a peptide that resists enzymatic breakdown in neural tissue longer than standard Semax, translating to an estimated 3 to 5 times greater potency per microgram. In practice, experienced nootropic users dose 100 to 300 mcg intranasally each morning for 10 to 20 day cycles. The peptide activates melanocortin receptors (MC3R, MC4R) and upregulates both BDNF and NGF in the basal forebrain. It also modulates serotonergic, dopaminergic, and enkephalin signaling pathways. Community reports across roughly 50 to 100 Reddit threads describe improved verbal fluency, working memory, and stress resilience within the first few days, with peak cognitive effects by days 7 to 10. The honest picture: zero human clinical trials exist for NA-Semax Amidate specifically. Every mechanistic citation traces back to the parent compound. PubMed returns about 12 results for "N-acetyl Semax" compared to roughly 150 for standard Semax. The potency multiplier is a pharmacokinetic inference, not a validated human comparison. Community experience across users who dose correctly has been consistently positive, but this is a preclinical compound with community-derived dosing.

NA-Semax Amidate is a synthetic analog of ACTH(4-10) extended with a Pro-Gly-Pro tripeptide tail. It activates melanocortin receptors MC3R and MC4R in the brain without triggering adrenal cortisol release, which separates it from full-length ACTH. The primary neurotrophic action comes through BDNF upregulation. Dolotov and colleagues showed that a single application of Semax at 50 mcg/kg produced a 1.4-fold increase in BDNF protein and a 3-fold increase in exon III BDNF mRNA in the hippocampus [1]. TrkB receptor phosphorylation increased 1.6-fold in the same study. A separate group confirmed that Semax raises NGF levels in the basal forebrain [2]. Beyond neurotrophins, the peptide modulates serotonergic, dopaminergic, and enkephalin (opioid) signaling systems. This multi-pathway engagement likely explains the combined cognitive and mood effects that community users consistently describe. The N-acetyl and amide modifications don't change receptor binding. They increase resistance to aminopeptidase and carboxypeptidase degradation. Magrì and colleagues studied N-terminal acetylation of Semax directly [3]; it is one of the few peer-reviewed studies of the modification. The practical effect is extended duration of activity in neural tissue compared to the parent compound.
NA-Semax Amidate benefits center on neurotrophic upregulation and cognitive performance during short intranasal cycles.
Estimated 3 to 5 times more potent than standard Semax per microgram, meaning lower doses and shorter cycles can achieve equivalent or greater neurotrophic stimulation.

BDNF and NGF upregulation supports learning, memory consolidation, and neuroplasticity. Parent compound data shows 1.4-fold BDNF protein increase and 3-fold BDNF mRNA increase in rat hippocampus at 50 mcg/kg [1].

Neuroprotective effects confirmed in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion models. Genome-wide transcriptional analysis of Semax in focal ischemia identified changes in immune and vascular gene expression [4].

Mood stabilization and stress resilience through serotonin and dopamine pathway modulation. Community users report reduced anxiety at appropriate doses, improved motivation, and emotional steadiness during the cycle window.

Cognitive benefits persist 1 to 3 weeks after the cycle ends. BDNF and NGF protein levels remain raised post-cessation in rodent Semax models, making the off-period a productive continuation rather than a gap.
Users report 6 to 12 hours of cognitive effect per dose, compared to 2 to 4 hours with standard Semax. Onset is rapid at 5 to 15 minutes intranasal.
Partially Aligned
Scientific Evidence
Based on 5 key studies · Research only
No human clinical trials exist for NA-Semax Amidate specifically.
Dosing studied: Not established in humans. Rodent Semax precedent: 50 mcg/kg intranasal. No validated human equivalent dose for the amidate form. All human dosing is community-derived extrapolation.

All mechanistic evidence derives from the parent compound Semax: approved in Russia for cognitive/neuroprotective indications and studied in human ischemia settings. The N-acetyl + C-terminal amide modifications are pharmacokinetically rational (protease resistance, extended intraneural duration) but unstudied in humans as a distinct compound. The 3–5× potency multiplier quoted here is a pharmacokinetic inference, not a formally validated human potency comparison.
Key Study

Dolotov et al. 2006 (PMID 16996037): Semax produces 3-fold BDNF mRNA increase and 1.6-fold TrkB phosphorylation in rat hippocampus at 50 mcg/kg (parent compound, not NA-Semax Amidate). For the acetylation itself, Magrì et al. 2016 (PMID 27586814) found that N-terminal acetylation changes how Semax binds copper. In neuroblastoma cells, the acetylated form did not protect against copper toxicity. It is one of the few peer-reviewed studies of the modification.
Limitations

No human RCTs for NA-Semax Amidate. PubMed count ~12 for "N-acetyl Semax" vs ~150 for parent Semax: extreme evidence gap for the modified form. Four of its five references are for parent Semax; the fifth studies N-acetyl Semax, and none tests the amidate form. Potency multiplier (3–5×) is a community estimate from pharmacokinetic reasoning, not a controlled human comparison. Its research status is preclinical.
Community Experience
Positive but niche.

Community dosing: 100–600 mcg/day intranasal; most users settle at 100–300 mcg. Few experienced users push to 600 mcg. Some sources note 900 mcg/day as an upper ceiling but this is rarely reported in practice.

Experienced nootropic users consistently report clear cognitive enhancement and mood stabilization at appropriate doses. Community consensus: superior duration and smoother profile than standard Semax at corrected dose. The #1 failure mode is treating it as equivalent-dose to parent Semax due to the 3–5× potency difference.

Community dosing, cycling rationale (10–20 day cycles), and route preference (intranasal) align with the Russian Semax clinical protocol tradition. Reported mechanism (BDNF upregulation, cognitive enhancement, neuroprotection) matches the validated parent compound mechanism. Divergent on the potency multiplier: community consensus of 3–5× is pharmacokinetically reasonable but not formally validated in humans. Science has no direct human data for NA-Semax Amidate; all parent-compound endorsement is inferred across the modification.

Start at 100 mcg intranasal, period. The potency mismatch with standard Semax is the number one user error. If you were running Semax at 300 mcg, your starting dose here is 100 mcg. Reconstitution math for intranasal: 10 mg vial plus 10 mL bacteriostatic water gives you 1 mg/mL (1000 mcg/mL). A standard nasal atomizer delivers about 0.1 mL per actuation, so each spray is 100 mcg. Three sprays gets you 300 mcg. Split across nostrils, wait 5 minutes between sides. For subcutaneous (less common): 10 mg vial plus 4 mL bacteriostatic water gives you 2.5 mg/mL. On a U-100 insulin syringe, 100 mcg is 4 IU, 300 mcg is 12 IU, 600 mcg is 24 IU. Dose before 10 AM. Nothing after 1 PM. The dopaminergic tail will wreck your sleep if you dose late. Refrigerate the reconstituted spray at 2 to 8 degrees C and toss it after 30 days. Lyophilized vials survive shipping better than pre-mixed sprays.
Cycling Protocol
Off Period
Standard protocol is 10-20 days on, 10-20 days off. Cognitive benefits often persist during the off period due to sustained BDNF elevation. Some users run 30-day cycles with longer breaks.
NA-Semax Amidate Cycle

Primary rationale from the original Russian Semax clinical protocols: cycling prevents melanocortin receptor (MC3R/MC4R) desensitization with sustained agonist exposure. Secondary: BDNF and NGF upregulation reaches a plateau within 10–20 days, making continued dosing yield diminishing returns while the neurotrophic benefits persist post-cessation: the off-period is a productive continuation of the effect, not a gap. Community users also cite a "fresh response" upon returning after the off-period as empirical evidence of receptor resensitization.
Diminishing cognitive response despite continued dosing at the same dose (BDNF/NGF plateau)
Increasing anxiety or irritability over consecutive days suggesting cumulative receptor activation
No additional subjective benefit perceived after day 10 of cycle at a stable dose

Overstimulation is the most reported problem with NA-Semax Amidate, and it is almost always self-inflicted. The compound is 3 to 5 times more potent per microgram than standard Semax. Users who transfer their parent compound dose directly (e.g. 300 mcg Semax mapped straight to 300 mcg NA-Semax Amidate) experience anxiety, agitation, and irritability. This is the number one failure mode cited across community reports. The anxiety response deserves emphasis. NA-Semax Amidate upregulates dopaminergic and serotonergic signaling. At higher doses, that stimulation tips from productive focus into agitation. Users with a history of anxiety disorders face increased risk; this compound is listed as contraindicated for severe anxiety disorders for exactly this reason. If anxiety appears, drop to 100 mcg and dose before 10 AM. Resolution typically happens within 1 to 2 days at the reduced dose. Sleep disruption ranks second among community complaints. The dopaminergic upregulation has a 6 to 12 hour activity tail. Dosing after 1 PM is the primary cause. Shifting the dose earlier in the morning typically resolves sleep disruption within 2 to 3 days. Hair thinning has been reported at sustained doses above 300 mcg per day over 30 or more days. The speculated mechanism involves melanocortin receptor (MC4R) activity. No clinical documentation exists for this effect; community reports indicate it reverses after cessation. The reports are rare. Nasal irritation can occur with intranasal use. Reconstituting above 2.5 mg/mL concentration increases irritation risk. Using a saline rinse before dosing helps. If irritation persists, subcutaneous injection is an alternative route. The human safety dataset is extremely limited. All published data comes from the parent compound Semax, not the amidate modification. PubMed returns about 12 results for the modified form. The researchStatus is correctly tagged as preclinical. No formal adverse event reporting exists. Contraindications include pregnancy, breastfeeding, known hypersensitivity to Semax or ACTH-derived peptides, active bleeding disorders, and history of severe anxiety disorders. If combining with MAO inhibitors, the risk of excessive monoamine accumulation and serotonin syndrome is real; that combination should be avoided. Stimulant medications (amphetamines, methylphenidate) carry additive CNS stimulation risk. Anticoagulant users should monitor closely given Semax's documented influence on vascular gene expression [4]. Stop use and consult a physician if new anxiety disorder symptoms appear, if insomnia persists despite timing adjustments, or if blood pressure exceeds 140/90 mmHg.
Common Issues & Solutions

Anxiety or overstimulation: Almost always a dose mismatch: this compound is 3–5× more potent than standard Semax. Users who transfer their Semax dose directly will overdose. Reduce to 100 mcg, dose before 10 AM, avoid all other stimulants. Resolution expected within 1–2 days at reduced dose.

Sleep disruption: Late dosing is the primary cause. The dopaminergic upregulation has a 6–12h activity tail. All doses must be taken before 1 PM. Shifting dose timing earlier typically resolves sleep disruption within 2–3 days.

No noticeable effect: Verify reconstitution: 10 mg vial in 10 mL BAC water = 1000 mcg/mL = 100 mcg per 0.10 mL actuation. Confirm the nasal spray device is delivering the correct volume. If using SubQ, consider switching to intranasal for superior direct CNS access. Allow 5–7 full days before evaluating efficacy.

Hair thinning (rare): Community-reported at sustained high doses (>300 mcg/day over 30+ days). Speculated mechanism: melanocortin receptor (MC4R) activity. No clinical documentation; appears reversible after cessation. Reduce dose or discontinue if observed.

Nasal irritation: Dilute the spray solution: standard is 1 mg/mL (10 mg in 10 mL); going above 2.5 mg/mL increases irritation risk. Saline rinse before dosing helps. If persistent, switch to SubQ route.

NA-Semax Amidate is classified as a research-only compound. It has no FDA approval, no IND application on record, and no regulatory pathway in progress in any Western jurisdiction. The parent compound Semax holds marketing authorization in Russia for cognitive and neuroprotective indications, but that approval does not extend to the N-acetyl amidated modification. In the United States, NA-Semax Amidate is sold online as a research chemical, labeled for in-vitro research purposes only. It is not approved for human use by any regulatory body. Compounding pharmacy availability does not apply to this compound. WADA status is uncertain. The parent compound Semax appears on some national anti-doping watchlists given its melanocortin receptor activity. Athletes subject to drug testing should treat this peptide as a risk. This content is for informational and educational purposes only. It does not constitute medical advice. Consult a licensed healthcare provider before using any research compound.

faqs.q: Is NA-Semax Amidate actually stronger than regular Semax?
faqs.a: Yes, roughly 3-5x more potent per microgram. The N-acetyl blocks aminopeptidase degradation and the C-terminal amide blocks carboxypeptidase. If you're used to 300 mcg of regular Semax, start NA-Semax Amidate at 100 mcg and work up slowly.

faqs.q: Why does NA-Semax Amidate make some people anxious?
faqs.a: Almost always a dosing issue. The dopaminergic and serotonergic upregulation at higher doses tips into agitation. Start at 100 mcg, dose before noon, and don't combine it with other stimulants. That fixes it for most people.

faqs.q: Can NA-Semax Amidate cause hair loss?
faqs.a: Some users on forums report it at higher doses over longer cycles, possibly related to melanocortin receptor (MC4R) activity. There's no clinical documentation and it appears rare. Reports suggest it reverses after stopping.

That follows the original Russian Semax clinical protocols. The cognitive benefits from BDNF and NGF upregulation persist 1-3 weeks after you stop, so longer continuous use gives diminishing returns. The off-period also prevents receptor desensitization.

faqs.q: Can I inject NA-Semax Amidate subcutaneously instead of using the nasal spray?
faqs.a: You can, but intranasal is preferred because the olfactory pathway gives direct CNS access. SubQ means the peptide has to cross the blood-brain barrier from systemic circulation, which likely reduces how much actually reaches the brain. Same mcg dosing applies for SubQ, but expect slower onset: about 30-45 minutes vs 5-15 minutes intranasal.

faqs.q: What is the recommended NA-Semax Amidate dosage?
faqs.a: NA-Semax Amidate dosing varies by experience level. Beginners typically start at 100 mcg daily, moderate users at 300 mcg daily, and aggressive protocols use 600 mcg daily.

faqs.q: How do you reconstitute NA-Semax Amidate?
faqs.a: NA-Semax Amidate typically comes in 10mg vials. Add 2mL of bacteriostatic water to the vial. Use the free calculator for exact syringe units based on your desired dose.

faqs.q: What is the half-life of NA-Semax Amidate?
faqs.a: The half-life of NA-Semax Amidate is ~5-10 min (intranasal). This determines how frequently you need to dose for consistent blood levels.

summary: . NA-Semax Amidate (N-Acetyl Semax Amidate) is the stabilized, higher-potency version of Russia's approved nootropic peptide. No human clinical trials exist for this specific modification. The cognitive benefits persist 1 to 3 weeks after you stop dosing, which is why cycles run just 10 to 20 days. Nootropic users who want sharper focus, better verbal fluency, and sustained BDNF elevation without daily long-term dosing tend to reach for this one.
